question: How CTrigger::LoadKey turns a key that is not one of its keywords into a condition, what the fifteen unread slot-7 LoadArgument bodies accept, what the block triggers' own keys take, and which keywords take a block of child triggers.

addresses.name: CTrigger::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CTrigger::LoadKey(CTrigger* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole trigger half of the event script language**, and the loader all 157 trigger classes inherit. One switch over the key's save token with **153 cases** (`port`, token 201, `CPortTrigger`, is the one FINDINGS-script.md's 152-row table lacks), each building the class that implements that keyword. A **leaf** case allocates, appends the child to `this`'s child list (16-byte node at +8/+0xC/+0x10) and calls the child's slot 7 `LoadArgument` with the value CToken copied from `parse +0x228` (tail 0x5C8E04). A **block** case - `and` `or` `not` `any_core` `any_neighbor_country` `any_neighbor_province` `any_owned_province` `enemy` `check_variable` `has_cb` `relation` `threat` `spy_mission_count` and, oddly, `has_hostile_spy_mission` - appends, sets the child's `is_script_block (+0x3C)` and calls the child's slot 3 `CPersistent::Load` (tail 0x5C914E), which reads `key = value` pairs to the closing brace through the child's own slot 4 - this function again for every CAndTrigger heir. **Neither tail tests the value's token**, so a block keyword written with a scalar swallows the rest of its enclosing block, and a leaf written with `{ }` ends its parent at its own closing brace.

The default arm (0x5CAD19), in order: (1) `Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey` (0x5CFD60) with the key text, the value text and `this->is_script_block` - a government position, a building, a technology, a unit type, a law group, a combined-arms unit group, each building its leaf and calling slot 7 with a CToken of class 0xF; a positive answer ends here. (2) An ideology by name (`GetIdeologies` + `CNameDataBase::GetByName`) - a 0x4C `CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger` loaded as a block. (3) A region name (`StringHashFind_At18` on `g_CMap +0x2A50`) - `CRegionScopeTrigger`, a block. (4) A trial scope rebinding (0x5CAE62) - `CContextTrigger`, a block. (5) Only if step 1 answered **0** - which it does when `is_script_block` is clear - `Unknown trigger-type <key> in <file>` through trigger.cpp line 0x10B on channel 0x10004. When `is_script_block` is set step 1 answers -1 after queuing the pair on `this`'s deferred lists, and an unrecognised key is then **dropped without a word** (replayed later only by CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys, which only technology loading calls).

Key tokens come from a case-insensitive ternary search tree (the text tokenizer's next-token, rva 0x66A2E0, looks every bare word up in g_dynamic_tokens through TernarySearchTreeFind), so `AND`, `Or`, `NOT`, `THIS`, `YES` are the keywords. Every lookup of the key's or value's **text** in the default arm and the LoadArgument bodies is case-sensitive (the engine string hash and a byte compare), except a country tag (CCountryDataBase::GetTag compares three characters with `_strnicmp` after hashing them case-sensitively). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9CAD19-0x9CAFA2 (the default arm and the error tail), the leaf tail 0x9C8E04-0x9C8E85 and the block tail 0x9C914E-0x9C91DF; every case's tail classified by script (wave/A/work/cases.py over switchmap.cases). The -1 path: 0x9CAD79 `test esi,esi; jg` falls on into the ideology arm, and 0x9CAEE3 `cmp [esp+0xc],0; jne` skips the error for any non-zero answer. Revised: the old comment said the default tried 'a province id, then an ideology, then the technology database' - the order and the list were both wrong. Would be shown wrong by a case whose tail is neither 0x9C8E04 nor 0x9C914E (none found among the 153).
addresses.revises: The default branch was described as 'a province id, then an ideology, then the technology database'. It is six database lookups (government position, building, technology, unit type, law group, unit group), then ideology, region, scope; the error is suppressed inside script-written blocks; and the leaf/block tails and the case rules are new.

addresses.name: Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey
addresses.signature: int __stdcall Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey(CTrigger* parent, Hoi3CString* key, Hoi3CString* value, bool defer)
addresses.comment:
**The first step of CTrigger::LoadKey's default arm: a key that names something in a database.** Tries the key text, case-sensitively, in this order, and on the first hit allocates 0x48 bytes, constructs the leaf, appends it to `parent`'s child list and calls its slot 7 (`LoadArgument`) with a CToken whose class is forced to **0xF** and whose text is `value` (snprintf "%s", 255 characters): (1) `g_government_positions` by name -> CGovernmentPositionTrigger; (2) `g_CBuildingDataBase` (StringHashFind_At1C) -> CBuildingTrigger; (3) the technology hash at `GetTechnologyDataBase() +0x10` -> CTechnologyTrigger; (4) `CSubUnitDataBase::by_name (+0x10)` through StringHashFind -> CSubUnitTrigger; (5) the law-group map at `GetLawDataBase() +0xC` (StringHashFind_At18) -> CLawTrigger, whose value is then a law name; (6) a combined-arms unit group (CSubUnitDataBase_FindUnitGroup, accepted only when the group's index at +0 is above 0) -> CCombinedArmsTrigger. Answers 1 on any of them. On none: if `defer` (the parent's `is_script_block`) it pushes `key` onto the parent's `deferred_keys (+0x1C)` and `value` onto `deferred_values (+0x2C)` and answers -1, else answers 0.

Because the CToken is class 0xF whatever the text, `THIS`/`FROM` never reach a CIntTrigger's flags through here (atoi gives 0), and `CCombinedArmsTrigger`'s `CBoolTrigger` slot 7 (`token == yes`) always stores **false**. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9CFD60-0x9D011E end to end: three exits all `ret 0x10`, `ebx = [ebp+8]` used as the child-list owner, the 0xA69470 token builder writing `mov [esi],0xF`. Constructors identified by the vftable each writes. Called from CTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5CAD5D (defer = movzx [ebx+0x3C]) and CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys at 0x5D01BA (defer = 0). Would be wrong if a second caller passed a different first argument than the trigger - findRefs shows only these two.

addresses.name: CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys
addresses.comment: **Replays the keys a script-written trigger block could not resolve when it was parsed.** Recurses over `children_first (+8)` first; then, when `is_script_block (+0x3C)` is set, walks `deferred_keys (+0x1C)` and `deferred_values (+0x2C)` (vectors of 0x1C-byte strings, counted with the /0x1C magic 0x92492493) and calls Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey(this, key, value, defer = 0) on each pair, logging `Fixed trigger dependency for K = V` (trigger.cpp line 0x16D, channel 0x10002) or `Failed to post process trigger dependency K = V` (line 0x16B, channel 0x10004); then clears both vectors. **Its only outside caller is in CTechnologyDataBase::LoadTechnologies (rva 0x14195C), over every technology's `allow` (+0x248)**, so a forward reference to a technology in a technology's allow is resolved here, and nothing replays the deferred keys of an event's or decision's trigger. The maintainer's own game.log carries 38 `Fixed trigger dependency` lines under the base game and 3306 under BlackICE (e.g. `infantry_activation = 1`, written directly in an allow in technologies/ArtilleryTechnologies.txt), and none of the failure line.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9D0130-0x9D03EA, bare `ret`, ecx = this (and recursion through `mov ecx,[ebx]; call 0x9d0130`). findRefs --callers 0x9D0130: 0x54195C and itself. The log lines are the live positive control for the line number 0x16D = 365 and the channel. Would be wrong if another trigger tree were walked by a second caller - only one outside caller exists.

addresses.name: StringVector_PushBack
addresses.comment: MSVC's `std::vector<std::string>::push_back`, statically linked with a register convention: the string in ECX, the vector `{first, last, end}` in EDI, 0x1C-byte elements; grows through 0x176F0 when `last == end` and handles the element-aliases-the-vector case. 201 direct callers. Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey uses it to queue a trigger key and its value on CTrigger +0x1C/+0x2C.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and read: [edi] first, [edi+4] last, [edi+8] end, stride 0x1C, std::string::assignString into the new slot, bare ret. findRefs --callers counts 201.

addresses.name: CSubUnitDataBase_FindUnitGroup
addresses.comment: **A combined-arms unit group by name**, out of the vector of group pointers at CSubUnitDataBase +0x0/+0x4 (common/combined_arms.txt's groups; name a std::string at group +8, compared byte for byte). Answers the group, or **the vector's first element** when no name matches. The group's dword at +0 is its one-based index, which is what CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey's `unit_group` case stores (rva 0x1A4CEB-0x1A4CF1, `mov edx,[eax]; mov [edi+0x1B4],edx`) and what Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey tests `> 0` to tell a real group from that fallback. Three callers: CSubUnitDefinition::LoadKey, CTechStatistics::LoadKey (rva 0x1388E9) and Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x5AE010-0x5AE0BB: `(end - begin) >> 2` count, element `[begin + i*4]`, name at element +8, both exits `ret 4`, the miss path `mov eax,[ebx]` with ebx = begin. FINDINGS-builders.md already said the groups are 'in a vector at its +0x00'.

addresses.name: CMap_FindContinent
addresses.comment: A continent by name: walks the vector of continent pointers at `CMap +0x2A30`/`+0x2A34`, asks each for its name through its slot 7 (a std::string returned by value) and compares byte for byte; answers the continent or null. CContinentTrigger::LoadArgument's lookup.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and the prologue disassembled: [ebp+8] is the map (reads +0x2A30), both exits `ret 8`, MemCompareRegs on the two strings with the length tie-break.

addresses.name: IdeologyGroup_FindByName
addresses.comment: An ideology **group** (`fascism`, `democracy`, `communism`) by name: a linear walk of the group vector at `g_ideologies +0x1C`/`+0x20`, the name a std::string at group +0x18, compared byte for byte; null on a miss. CIdeologyGroupTrigger::LoadArgument's lookup.

addresses.name: CControlledByTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment: Slot 7 for `controlled_by`: `this` -> `arg_is_this (+0x18)`; `from` -> `arg_is_from (+0x19)`; **`owner` (token 0x1EC) -> `is_owner (+0x48)` = 1**, the keyword that selects Evaluate's 'controller equals owner' arm; anything else -> CCountryDataBase::GetTag into `tag (+0x40/+0x44)`, `---`/0 for an unknown tag.

addresses.name: CDateTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment: Slot 7 for `date`: Date_SetFromString on `date (+0x40)` with the value text - `y.m.d.h`, sscanf with the result never tested, so text that is not a date gives a date before the epoch and no message.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled: `lea eax,[ebp+0xc]; lea esi,[ecx+0x40]; call 0x44cda0; ret 0x104`. Single holder.

addresses.name: CExistsTrigger::LoadArgument
addresses.comment: Slot 7 for `exists`: first `value (+0x40)` = 0 and `tag (+0x44/+0x48)` = `---`/0; then token `yes` -> `value` = 1; token `no` -> `value` = 0; anything else -> CCountryDataBase::GetTag into `tag`. So `exists = yes|no` asks about the scope's country and `exists = TAG` about the tag (Evaluate ignores `value` in that form). No THIS/FROM: `exists = THIS` is looked up as a tag and gives `---`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: the defaults, then tests 0x1F6 and 0x1F7. Single holder.

addresses.name: CFactionTrigger::LoadArgument

Finally a null `faction` is replaced by the CNullFaction singleton, so `faction` is never null. **`from` is not a keyword here**: `faction = FROM` is looked up as a faction name and gives CNullFaction.

addresses.name: CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger::LoadKey(CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **`<ideology> = { organisation = N popularity = N }`** - the block an ideology's name opens (CTrigger::LoadKey's default arm, after the database names). **Two keys, not one**: `organisation` (token 0x4C8) -> `organisation (+0x44)` and `popularity` (0x4FB) -> `popularity (+0x48)`, each `atoi(text) * 1000` **at load**, so no decimals. Any other key is ignored without a message. Both default to 0, and Evaluate is an OR of the two, so a block naming only one of them is always true.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9FA760-0x9FA7B1: `sub eax,0x4c8; je` -> +0x44, `sub eax,0x33; jne out` -> +0x48, both `imul eax,eax,0x3e8`. definitions.py had reported one key.
addresses.revises: Said one key, `popularity`. There are two, `organisation` and `popularity`, and both are scaled by 1000 here - not in Evaluate, as CThreatTrigger::Evaluate's comment says of this class.

addresses.name: CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: False when `ideology (+0x40)` is null; otherwise, with `i = ideology->+0x4C` and the scope's country, **`organisation_by_ideology (+0x10C4)[i] >= organisation (+0x44)` OR `popularity_by_ideology (+0x10FC)[i] >= popularity (+0x48)`**. So vanilla's coup events' `social_conservative = { organisation = 60 popularity = 60 }` holds when either figure reaches 60. Also an independent reading that +0x10C4 is organisation and +0x10FC popularity: each key is compared against its own array here.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9FA6B0-0x9FA75C, `ret 4`: both-pass -> true; else organisation alone -> true; else popularity alone -> true; else false. vtable.py --holding: CAllOrganisationPopularityTrigger slot 6 only.

addresses.name: CMTTHModifier::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CMTTHModifier::LoadKey(CMTTHModifier* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **A mean-time-to-happen `modifier = { factor = F <conditions> }`.** `factor` -> ParseFixedPoint into `factor (+0x40)`, thousandths with decimals; **every other key goes to CTrigger::LoadKey on the modifier**, so the rest of the block is an implicit AND of ordinary triggers with the whole trigger grammar.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: `if (key != factor) CTrigger::LoadKey(this, parse, key)` else ParseFixedPoint.
addresses.revises: The comment was definitions.py's 'keys its switch names: factor'; it now says what factor is parsed as and that every other key is a condition.

addresses.name: COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: **`owned_by`** - CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFAB0) with `CProvince::owner_id (+0x330)` where that one reads `controller_id (+0x338)`, but with **three** argument forms, not four: `this`, `from` and a literal tag at `+0x44`. There is no keyword arm - the object is 0x48 bytes, so it has no +0x48 flag - and `owned_by = owner` is looked up as a tag, gives `---`/0, and holds only for an unowned province. Same `return false` when the scope names no province. Its slot 7 loader is the shared 0x5E8F40, which is what puts the tag at `+0x40`/`+0x44` and sets `arg_is_this`/`arg_is_from`.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9DF250-0x9DF39C: three exits returning true (0x9DF338, 0x9DF365, 0x9DF386) and one false, with no read of +0x48 anywhere; CTrigger::LoadKey allocates it with `push 0x48`.

addresses.name: CLawTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `<law_group> = <law>`: true when the scope country's `laws (+0x628)` entry at `law_group (+0x40) ->+0x50` (the group's index) **is** `law (+0x44)`. An unknown law leaves CNullLaw there, which no country holds once its laws are set.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9FBD40-0x9FBD7F, `ret 4`, `cmp edx,[ecx+0x44]; sete al`. vtable.py --holding: CLawTrigger slot 6 only.

addresses.name: CCombinedArmsTrigger::Evaluate
addresses.comment: `<unit_group> = yes|no` (`armor_unit_type` and the other common/combined_arms.txt names) inside a combat. False with no `combatant (+0x40)` or when the combatant's slot 6 answers false; then over the combatant's units (`+0x40` list): with `value (+0x40)` set, true if **some** unit's presence vector (`+0x1D0`) is non-zero at the group's index; with it clear, true if **none** is. **The parser always stores it clear** - Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey hands slot 7 a class-0xF token, never `yes` - so the form as written means "this side has no unit of the group", whatever its value. Neither vanilla nor BlackICE uses it.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0xA07A00-0xA07A8A, two loops split on `cmp byte [edi+0x40],0`; vtable.py --holding: CCombinedArmsTrigger slot 6 only. The usage negative: grep for `(infantry|armor|artillery|direct_fire|support)_unit_type =` over events, decisions and common of both trees finds only combined_arms.txt's own definitions.

addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x9EBA90-0x9EBAEF: `mov ecx,[eax+0x12c]; mov eax,[edx+0x20]; call eax`; CLeader slot 8 is 0xA92590 (`mov al,1; ret`), CNullLeader's 0x592360 (`xor al,al; ret`). Slot 7 of the table is 0x415FF0.

struct_fields.name: is_script_block
struct_fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set.
struct_fields.evidence: Writers (rvas): 0x5C915B (block tail), 0x5CAE09 (default-arm tail), 0x133B39/0x133B32 in the function at 0x1339A0 (technology +0x284 and +0x314, i.e. +0x248+0x3C and +0x2D8+0x3C). Readers: 0x5CAD4F (pushed as Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey's defer flag) and 0x5D0171 (ResolveDeferredKeys' gate). Positive control: game.log's 'Fixed trigger dependency for infantry_activation = 1', a key written directly in a technology's allow.
